cards.text: Near the end of the book of Micah, the message has just mourned that no one upright is left (Micah 7:2). Then the speaker says, "I will wait for the God of my salvation…" (Micah 7:7). Now the message turns to an enemy: "Do not gloat over me, my enemy!"

cards.question: True or false: the speaker tells the enemy that after falling, there's no getting back up.
Sitting in darkness, the speaker says the LORD will be a ___.

cards.text: Then the speaker owns it: "Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD…" No excuses, no "traffic was CRAZY."

cards.question: The speaker must endure the LORD's rage. Until when?

answers.text: Until the LORD argues the case
Until every debt is paid back

cards.text: But the rage isn't the last word. The speaker says the LORD will execute justice and bring the speaker into the light.

cards.question: When the enemy who said, "Where is the LORD your God?" sees what happens, what covers her?

cards.text: The speaker says that at that time she'll be trampled like mud in the streets. She went from trash-talking to TRAMPLED, friend.

cards.question: Then the message turns to "you": the day will come for ___ your walls and extending your boundary.

cards.text: On that day, the message says, they will come to you from Assyria, a powerful empire, and from the cities of Egypt, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain. That's not a guest list, friend, that's the WHOLE MAP.

cards.question: Then the message says the earth will become desolate. Why?

answers.text: Because of what its people did
Because its walls were never built

cards.text: Then the message turns to God: shepherd Your people with Your staff, the flock of Your inheritance, and let them graze in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old. Asking for the good old days back? Believe me, friend, a stamper who spent years in a junk drawer KNOWS that feeling.

cards.question: Then the message looks back: as in the days of coming out of Egypt, ___ will be shown.

cards.text: The nations will see and be ashamed, stripped of all their might, hands over their mouths and ears gone deaf. You know the face somebody makes right after hitting "reply all" by accident? THAT face.

cards.question: The nations will lick the dust like a snake. True or false: they will also come trembling from their strongholds in fear of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the message asks the big one: "Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance…" Go ahead, look around, friend, nobody's raising their hand.

cards.question: The message says God does not hold on to His anger forever. Why not?

answers.text: His people finally earned His favor

cards.text: Then the message says, "He will again have compassion on us; He will vanquish our iniquities." Notice that word, friend: not "them," US.

cards.question: Then the message pictures God casting out all our sins. Where do they go?

answers.text: Into the depths of the sea

cards.question: The message ends by saying God will show faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, Israel's forefathers. True or false: it calls this something new that God never promised before.
